summary: Round 32 recheck, 03:13-04:15Z 29 Sep. I made no Kaggle calls and used no browser; everything here is local. At the 03:14Z poll, night probes 52-54 are PENDING, and the 02:27Z feed shows no new topic and no E10. Before choosing, I audited all 94 earlier recheck items (rounds 2-31), ideas_29sep and knobarms_28sep. Almost every v2/v3/RESULTS idea is already covered. The three I picked have never been rechecked by name, and I measured each one on the exp60 x138 lab (56 clips, 99 GT divisions, CPU). (A) v2 'insert-at-ckpt' means running DaughterNet insertion before the short-track filter. The code does run insertion after the filter (exp85a l.4672-4677), so the mechanism is real. But only 3 of 99 GT divisions lose a daughter to the filter while the parent survives, and all 3 are 45-75 frames from the clip end, so there is no clip-end blind zone. The ceiling is about +0.0023 lab at perfect ranking, and it cannot be replayed (the deleted fragments were never DaughterNet-scored). It STAYS CLOSED for 29 Sep and is a small post-deadline item. (B) v3 (i) 'LoG shoulders' was refuted on global node recall (+0.0002). It was never aimed at the division class it fits: in 9 of 85 lab FN divisions (11%), one predicted node covers BOTH GT daughters (GT sister median 5.97 um, just after cytokinesis). The verdict for 29 Sep is unchanged (new GPU code at a fragile anchor, no lab, no slot). The post-deadline target changes from global recall to a 'split the merged daughter' step, with a ceiling of 9 division TP in the lab (~+0.007 at perfect precision) and a realistic ~20% capture from v3's own toy. (C) The v2-dropped linajea parent-vector head was dropped as 'cheaper division levers first'. Those levers are now spent: the public orphan-volume dose peaks at cap 6 (0.954 / 0.956 / 0.955 / 0.955, thr 0.3 no UP), and the lab's orphan pool is used up by cap 24. The remaining lab division FN are 40% claimed daughters and 11% merged, and only a parentage or split signal reaches them. For 29 Sep it stays closed (training). Post-deadline, it merges into R22's theft-aware ranker as the image-evidence version and ranks first on the division agenda. None of the three changes the MORNING TABLE, the night reads or the finals card. Plan issue: 7 rounds of rechecks (R25-R31, 21 items) produced info lines only. I suggest pausing the recheck lens for the remaining 29 Sep rounds, or pointing it only at claims on the 12:03Z / 18:37Z finals card.

findings.what: v2 'insert-at-ckpt' is arm (c) of div-cap-private-J (research/wf_ideas_v2/r1_dedupe.json). The idea: an extra DaughterNet insertion pass BEFORE the short-track filter, to rescue ~10 daughters the filter deletes. OLD VERDICT: dropped with the rest of div-cap-private-J (v2 FINAL_REPORT Dropped: 'beyond cap 4 the marginal is 0 TP / +2 FP'). The arm needed a GPU DaughterNet run for nodes missing from the export. It was never measured on x138, and no v4 round rechecked it. WHAT CHANGED: (1) Division insertion is now the lead LB-positive family (cap 4 +0.001, cap 6 +0.002; probes 35/45). (2) The code order is confirmed in every current file (exp85a post cell l.4663-4717): safe-div -> geometry filter -> prune_isolated -> filter_short_track_components (MIN_TRACK_LEN 6; keeps components that contain a fork) -> linefit -> divinsert. A true daughter on a short orphan fragment (< 6 nodes) is deleted before the insertion can attach it. If it were attached first, the fork would keep its component. MEASURED (exp60 lab, x138 control, nearest node <= 7 um at the same t): of 99 GT divisions, only 3 have a daughter matched solely by a node the short filter removed while the parent survives (6bba_268e1230 t24, 6bba_afb141ff t47, 6bba_fc5f39dc t54), plus 1 with no parent. The clips end at t = 99, so all 3 are 45-75 frames from the end: there is no clip-end blind zone. By comparison, 72 FN have both daughters present. NEW VERDICT: the mechanism is real but small, and it STAYS CLOSED for 29 Sep. The ceiling is 3 division TP, ~+0.0008 each on the ins35 lab base (J 0.192), so <= +0.0023 lab pooled at perfect ranking. That is before the new FP candidates that every short fragment would add to the orphan pool. It cannot be replayed on CPU, because the divins dump holds DaughterNet p only for final-graph triples. It would be new tail code after R8, with a changed DaughterNet workload (and so runtime) and no slot. It refines R22-RC-B's 'one daughter undetected 21' class: 3 of those daughters were detected and then filtered.

findings.what: v3 FINAL_REPORT (i) 'LoG-shoulders: +0.0002 on top of a line that is itself unlikely to ship' (v_literature_log-shoulder-hypotheses_value/schedule). OLD VERDICT/EVIDENCE: valued on GLOBAL missing-node recall (a_never 1,907 FN, mostly 6bba density misses). A toy check showed -LoG at sigma 1 voxel creates the missing 2nd peak in 2/10 merged 1D configs and rescues 12/60 z-merged 3D configs (20%). The host line (byteext / low-score pool) was expected not to ship. The lowdet anchor has a silent-collision history (x138 cell 4). WHAT CHANGED: (1) The host premise moved: probe 50 READMIT 0.94 read '+' for end-anchored low-score nodes (R26-RC-B). (2) The division term is where the LB now pays (cap 6, K), and the idea was never aimed there. MEASURED (exp60 lab, control): in 9 of the 85 FN divisions whose parent and both daughters are matched (11%), ONE predicted node matches BOTH GT daughters. The GT sister distance is median 5.97 um (2.87-7.85), i.e. daughters just after cytokinesis inside one blob, ~1.8-4.8 voxels apart on the 1.625 um grid. No insertion, steal or cap knob can fix these, because there is no second node to attach. This is the case class on which v3's mirror/lowdet-daughter was rejected ('c1 is often the merged blob'). NEW VERDICT: the 29 Sep verdict is UPHELD: new GPU-side code at the lowdet anchor, no lab replay (the lab has no heatmaps), no slot, after R8. The post-deadline verdict CHANGES from 'global recall +0.0002, dominated' to a narrow 'merged-daughter splitter' at t+1 of a parent track. Ceiling 9 lab division TP (~+0.007 at perfect precision). Realistic capture ~20% by the v3 toy, so ~2 TP (~+0.0015 lab), minus split FPs. A sister floor >= 5 um would already exclude 2-3 of the 9. It is distinct from the closed z-split (R7-RC-B), which was global and z-only.

findings.what: v2 r1_dedupe dropped 'linajea-parent-vector-head' (a per-node regressor of the offset to the parent at t-1). OLD VERDICT: 'Needs the capture plus training of a new regressor (with t-1 features), and its main payoff is the division term, where public J rests on perhaps 10-30 events (+-0.003 per event). The cheaper division levers (cap ...) first.' WHAT CHANGED: (1) The cheaper levers are SPENT on the public board. The orphan-insertion dose peaks at cap 6: #37 cap 4 0.954, exp70g cap 6 0.956, exp78a cap 8 0.955, exp78b cap 12+fc2 0.955, exp70q thr 0.3 0.956 with no UP; S1 closed DIV volume. K (ILP_DIVISION_WEIGHT 0.4 + READMIT) was the last knob. (2) The division term is live on public: two volume reads moved the display, while the lab under-valued forks (R20-RC-A). (3) MEASURED anatomy of the 85 lab FN divisions with parent and both daughters matched (control, no insertion): 34 claimed (40%: the 2nd daughter is linked from another track), 27 orphan (32%: DaughterNet's pool, all scored, 11 of 22 fully scored triples >= 0.4, used up by cap 24 fc2 per R22-NF), 9 merged into one node (11%, R32-RC-B), 2 other. Separately, 3 were filter-deleted (R32-RC-A) and ~10 never detected. So ~half of the remaining division mass (claimed + merged) cannot be reached by any existing knob. For the claimed class, the question is 'which parent does this node come from', which is exactly what a parent-vector head answers from the image, where R22's theft-aware ranker would answer from graph features. NEW VERDICT: for 29 Sep, UPHELD closed (training, capture, R8, no slot). The dropping REASON is void: the cheaper levers have been run and have plateaued. Post-deadline, it MERGES with R22-RC-B's theft-aware ranker as its image-evidence variant and ranks at the top of the division agenda, ahead of DaughterNet volume and wider gates. Caveat: the lab is in-sample and under-valued forks on public, so the counts are structural but their public worth is not.
